title: Revocation and Key Compromise Provisions
content:
Subscriber agreement provisions on revocation for SSL/TLS Certificates issued through Harborline Hosting & Domains.

**Provision 1 — Revocation at the subscriber's request.** The subscriber may have the certificate revoked at any time, at the product's revocation fee. A revocation that ends the subscription refunds nothing, save where the certificate refund terms themselves provide a refund.

**Provision 2 — Compromised private key.** When the private key is compromised, the current certificate is revoked. Where the product provides replacement after key compromise, a replacement is issued as a free reissue under a new key while the subscription continues.

**Provision 3 — Certificate Transparency.** Every issued certificate is logged to Certificate Transparency where the product logs certificates to public Certificate Transparency logs.

**Provision 4 — No reactivation.** A revoked subscription cannot be reactivated.

### The provisions side by side

| Event | Certificate | Subscription | Money |
|---|---|---|---|
| revocation at the subscriber's request that ends the subscription | revoked | ended; cannot be reactivated | the product's revocation fee; nothing refunded save under the refund terms |
| key compromise, product with replacement after key compromise | current certificate revoked; free reissue under a new key | continues | no reissue charge |

### Illustration (hypothetical)

A hypothetical subscriber reports that the private key behind a Harborline OV Single Domain certificate has been exposed. The current certificate is revoked, a replacement is issued as a free reissue under a new key, the subscription runs on to its end date, and the replacement is logged to Certificate Transparency like every issued certificate. Had the subscriber instead asked for revocation to end the subscription, the subscription could not later be reactivated.
